source: PROVISIONAL. The phase names and cues follow the two-hand catch as commonly coached. The numeric bands are placeholders chosen to be wider than the 5 degree measurement threshold. They are NOT coaching-approved. Replace them from the Netball Skills and Conditioning Manual and a coach review before any of this is shown to an athlete.

checkpoints.cue: Start with soft elbows, hands in front of the chest.
checkpoints.why: A locked arm cannot absorb the ball and transmits the impact to the shoulder.

checkpoints.cue: Hands up and ready, not hanging at your sides.
checkpoints.why: A low starting position costs time that the reach cannot recover.

checkpoints.cue: Reach to the ball early. Meet it, do not wait for it.
checkpoints.why: Catching early wins the contest and protects possession.

checkpoints.cue: Take the ball with bent elbows so you can give with it.
checkpoints.why: Bent elbows at contact give the range needed to absorb the ball.

checkpoints.cue: Both hands work together. Match your hands.
checkpoints.why: One dominant hand turns a two-hand catch into a one-hand catch.

checkpoints.cue: Meet the ball out in front, at chest height or above.
checkpoints.why: Contact close to the body removes the room needed to absorb the ball.

checkpoints.cue: Draw the ball in to your chest and secure it.
checkpoints.why: Pulling the ball in absorbs the momentum and protects it from a defender.

checkpoints.cue: Bring your hands back down to a strong, balanced position.
checkpoints.why: Finishing high leaves the ball exposed and the next pass slow.
